scope.current_boundary: Teach ideal gas definition as obeying pV proportional to T where T is thermodynamic temperature, equation of state pV = nRT and pV = NkT, relation k = R / N_A, thermodynamic temperature scale and absolute zero, and changes of state. Do not pre-teach kinetic theory assumptions, molecular derivation pV = (1/3)Nm<c^2>, r.m.s. speed, or molecular kinetic energy (1/2)m<c^2> = (3/2)kT.
prior_scope_summaries_consulted: Assumes mastery of amount of substance, the mole, Avogadro constant N_A, and particle-mole conversions from lesson 9702_t15_cm01_l01.

immediate_previous.boundary: Amount of substance as an SI base quantity with base unit mol, the mole, the Avogadro constant N_A, elementary entities, molar mass, and calculating particle count from mass and moles.
can_assume: amount of substance n in moles
molar mass M and particle mass m = M / N_A

immediate_next.boundary: Basic assumptions of kinetic theory of gases and derivation of pV = (1/3)Nm<c^2>.
must_not_preteach: kinetic theory assumptions (negligible volume of molecules, no intermolecular forces, elastic collisions, random motion, negligible collision time)

selection_dimensions: P4 examination parts assessing definition of ideal gas, thermodynamic temperature, pV = nRT calculations, pV = NkT calculations, and relation k = R / N_A across multiple exam series (2016 to 2024).

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Assesses the definition of an ideal gas: gas that obeys pV proportional to T for all values of p, V and T where T is thermodynamic temperature [2 marks].
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: State what is meant by an ideal gas [2 marks].
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Mark 1 for pV proportional to T, Mark 2 for thermodynamic temperature. Omitting thermodynamic loses the second mark.

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Assesses the exact temperature of absolute zero in degrees Celsius (-273.15 °C).
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: State the temperature, in degrees Celsius, of absolute zero [1 mark].

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Assesses direct calculation of number of molecules N using pV = NkT with temperature given in Celsius.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Calculate the number of molecules of gas in the vessel [3 marks].
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Requires conversion of 227 °C to 500 K and substitution into pV = NkT with Boltzmann constant k = 1.38e-23. Informed Worked Example 2 and Guided practice.
lesson_sections_informed: The ideal gas equation: molecular form (pV = NkT)
Worked Example 2: Molecular calculations and molecular mass from pV = NkT

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Assesses calculating the mass of a single molecule from total mass and calculated molecule count N.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Calculate the mass of one molecule of the gas [1 mark].
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Tests m = m_total / N. Informed Worked Example 2 Part 2.
lesson_sections_informed: Worked Example 2: Molecular calculations and molecular mass from pV = NkT

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Assesses rearrangement of pV = nRT to find thermodynamic temperature T, testing volume conversion from cm^3 to m^3.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Determine the temperature of the gas given moles, pressure, and volume in cm^3 [2 marks].
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: M1 for pV = nRT; A1 for T = 500 K. Common error is forgetting 10^-6 factor on cm^3. Informed Worked Example 1 and Mistake 2.
lesson_sections_informed: The ideal gas equation: molar form (pV = nRT)
Worked Example 1: State parameters, moles, and isochoric heating

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Assesses Charles's law (V / T = constant) during constant-pressure heating.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Use answer in (a) to determine new volume of gas after temperature rises by 125 K at constant pressure [2 marks].
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: B1 for V / T is constant; A1 for new volume. Informed empirical gas laws and proportional reasoning sections.
lesson_sections_informed: Empirical gas laws leading to the equation of state
Worked Example 1: State parameters, moles, and isochoric heating

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Assesses calculation of molecule count N from pV = NkT at room temperature (21 °C = 294 K).
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Calculate the number N of molecules in the gas [2 marks].
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Accepts pV = NkT or pV = nRT followed by N = n * N_A. Emphasizes interchangeability of both equations of state.
lesson_sections_informed: The ideal gas equation: molecular form (pV = NkT)

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Assesses extracting p, V, T data from a state table and calculating amount n of gas in moles.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Calculate the amount n of gas [2 marks].
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: C1 for substitution into pV = nRT; A1 for n = 0.14 mol.
lesson_sections_informed: The ideal gas equation: molar form (pV = nRT)

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Directly assesses outcome 9702_t15_m02_o03: recalling the relation between N_A, R, and k.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: State the relationship between the Avogadro constant NA, molar gas constant R, and Boltzmann constant k [1 mark].
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: B1 for N_A = R / k or k = R / N_A. Informed Boltzmann constant section and Active Learning Check 2.

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Assesses show calculation for n = 150 mol using pV = nRT with temperature 17 °C = 290 K and volume in cm^3.
